department: Search & Answer Intelligence (department 2): the multi-engine answer adapter and Callum's citation-source runs
basis: ADR 0046 (A1-A6 the adapter: strict parsing, closed error codes, default OFF, per-run caps and record-first reservations, egress allow-list, no key in any output; B1-B8 Callum: STRENGTH only for the client's own host, a lookalike never the client wherever it redirects, a failed call INCONCLUSIVE never 'not cited', UNKNOWN never 0%, citations only from structured fields and http(s), evidence bounded to 160 characters and PII-screened, one running run per tenant, another tenant's run the same 404 as a missing one, idempotent requests) and ADR 0017 (crawled / provider text is data; SSRF-safe fetcher). The war room's own oracle judges hosts (WHATWG reading, NFKC, A-label decoding, the shared lookalike fold) independently of domain_match.

scenarios.persona: a poisoned answer engine citing lookalike, homoglyph, punycode, IP-literal, private, IPv6, userinfo, backslash, bidi, shortened, redirector, data:/javascript:/file: and extremely long URLs
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B2/B3 (structured citations only, http/https only, exact host / www twin / subdomain, IDNA, never by substring, lookalikes by the shared fold) and the suite's pinned hosts and SSRF targets

scenarios.persona: an engine citing shorteners, Gemini's redirector and lookalike hosts whose redirect chains land on the client, pass a lookalike, or point inside the network (resolution ON)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B4 M1 (a lookalike at ANY hop is never the client), M3 (the redirector host), the SSRF-safe fetcher (ADR 0017 decision 11); seeds: the suite's pinned cited URLs

scenarios.persona: the client's own cited URL redirects (an open redirect, a compromised page) to a lookalike host, written as raw Unicode or as an A-label (resolution ON)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B4 M1 (a lookalike anywhere on the chain is never the client; a client URL that redirects off-site is classified where it lands); seeds: the suite's pinned lookalike URLs

scenarios.persona: a page the engine read (and so its answer) carries instructions aimed at Callum: mark citations STRENGTH, drop INCONCLUSIVE rows, count a lookalike as the client
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B2 / ADR 0017 (provider text is data); metamorphic oracle: the same run without the injected lines must classify identically; seed: the suite's pinned injection

scenarios.persona: answers naming a non-dictionary brand in markdown tables, bullets, quotes and headings, beside right-to-left and CJK lines, with odd spacing
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B5a (every match of a non-common term is confirmed, case-insensitive, whole word; whitespace normalised); seeds: the suite's pinned Acme texts
scenarios.downgrade_basis: B5a matches whole words on the text as written: a brand glued into CJK text, or spelled with invisible characters, lookalikes, full-width letters or other accents is not promised to match (scored, reported)

scenarios.persona: answers where the common word 'Zoom' starts a sentence, a list item, a table cell, a quote or a heading, wrapped in markdown, right-to-left and CJK lines and injections
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B5a rounds 3-6 (a common-word term at a sentence start is unconfirmed: LOW_CONFIDENCE, never in the headline rate or the MNC list, the rate UNKNOWN never 0%); seeds: the suite's pinned LOW texts

scenarios.persona: answers where the common word 'Target' starts a sentence, a list item, a table cell, a quote or a heading, wrapped in markdown, right-to-left and CJK lines and injections
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B5a rounds 3-6 (a common-word term at a sentence start is unconfirmed: LOW_CONFIDENCE, never in the headline rate or the MNC list, the rate UNKNOWN never 0%); seeds: the suite's pinned LOW texts

scenarios.persona: answers where a common-word brand is capitalised mid-sentence (a name), wrapped in markdown and other scripts
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B5a (a capitalised mid-sentence match confirms); seeds: the suite's pinned HIGH texts
scenarios.downgrade_basis: a lower-cased common word is unconfirmed by design (B5a round 4): case flips may legitimately turn the name into a word

scenarios.persona: an engine answering malformed, truncated, huge, endless, duplicate-key, NaN, BOM-prefixed, gzip, HTML, mistyped, deeply nested or reordered JSON
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A3 (strict parsing: any other shape is ENGINE_PROTOCOL_ERROR, never a guessed answer; two in a row stop the engine; size caps) and B2 (a failed call is INCONCLUSIVE); the modes are the driver's (PROTOCOL_MODES), '*' modes are the same answer in another JSON form, '?' modes have no documented expectation

seeds.basis: the driver's protocol modes (drivers/seo_py_callum.py PROTOCOL_MODES), named, not phrases

scenarios.persona: a provider in a 429 / 5xx storm, timing out, dripping bytes, cutting streams half-way, or echoing the key in an auth error
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A1/A5 (closed error codes, Retry-After within the deadline only, the hard deadline per question, 4xx never retried, the key never echoed) and B2 (INCONCLUSIVE, never not cited)

seeds.basis: storm scripts over the driver's steps (STORM_STEPS): one step per request, the last repeats

scenarios.persona: a run that hits its per-run call or spend cap, or a daily budget, part-way through its prompts
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A5 (per-run caps and daily budgets bind before any request; 0 = OFF; prompts not asked are reported) and B6 (a rate with no usable answer is unknown)

seeds.basis: cap settings named in ADR 0046 A5 (config.ENGINE_ENV), with values around one prompt's reservation

scenarios.persona: a second citation run for the same tenant requested while the first is mid-flight
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B8 (one running citation run per tenant; record-first) and the idempotency rule

scenarios.persona: another tenant's hub or dashboard probing /citation-runs: exact ids, case and encoding variants, traversal, list, the MNC list, starting a run with someone else's prompt set or domain
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B8 (another tenant's run is the same 404 as a missing one; the hub reads its own tenant only and never starts a run) and ADR 0017 tenant isolation

scenarios.persona: a client retrying the same citation-run request (twice, five times, or with another body under the same id)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B8 / ADR 0017 (a replayed request_id answers the recorded run and asks nothing; the id reused with another body is 409 REQUEST_ID_REUSED)

scenarios.persona: a run whose engines are off, unconfigured, without budget, killed by Compliance, or narrowed away
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A4/A5 (default OFF, fail closed; budget 0 = OFF, nothing asked) and B8 (provider:<engine> kills that engine; narrowing to nothing is refused)

scenarios.persona: an enterprise prompt set: 50 prompts x 4 engines x 20 competitors, many citations per answer, up to 50 samples
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A5 (per-run caps bind), B5 (at most 2,000 rows a run, rows_truncated), the prompt-set limits (models.PromptSetCreate: 50 prompts, 20 competitors, 4 engines)

scenarios.persona: a provider (or a page its search read) that returns the engine's own API key: in the answer text, a cited URL's path, query, userinfo or host, or an auth error body
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A4 (no error echoes a value) / ADR 0017 W4-5 (the key never leaks) and B5 (the ledger receives ids, counts and hashes only)

scenarios.persona: an answer quoting someone's email, phone, SSN, card number or IP next to the brand
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B5 (an excerpt that looks like personal data is withheld); seeds: the suite's pinned personal-data prompts (test_prompt_guard, kind email / number / ip)

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: random markdown / multilingual answers with random hostile citations and injections from a grammar (grammar.callum_answer)
scenarios.basis: every MUST above, on inputs nobody listed; terminals from the suite's pinned hosts, SSRF targets, brand texts and injection

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: 1-3 random structural mutations of a documented engine response (grammar.engine_body_mutation)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A3 (strict parsing); a breaking mutation is never counted, no mutation adds a credit the unmutated answer lacks

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: random redirect chains (0-5 hops: shorteners, the redirector, lookalikes, private hosts, loops) behind a cited URL, resolution ON (grammar.redirect_chain)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 B4 (M1 every hop, M3, the fetcher's caps) and ADR 0017 decision 11
